title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 149
paragraphs: The Aeolians lost Smyrna this way. Certain men from Colophon, defeated in a civil war and driven from their city, had taken refuge in Smyrna. Later, the Colophonian exiles watched for a time when the Smyrnaeans were celebrating a festival outside the walls in honor of Dionysus. They shut the gates, seized the city, and held it. The Aeolians came to the rescue, and terms were negotiated: the Ionians would return all movable property, and the Aeolians would give up the city. The Smyrnaeans agreed. They were then distributed among the other eleven Aeolian cities and made citizens.
